judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer newsletter text input (#newsletter-input-name, type=text, name=newsletter, label and placeholder 'Digite seu nome'). It has no autocomplete attribute in the snapshot's rendered DOM, and the live server-rendered HTML fetched on 2026-11-25 has the same markup with no autocomplete anywhere in the form, so the capture does not differ. claimTrue is cannot_tell only because 'nome' may mean the full name (token 'name') rather than the first name ('given-name') the claim asserts; the part that it does not identify its purpose holds. Reasons a skeptic could raise do not hold: the field collects the user's own name for a sign-up, a purpose listed in Input Purposes; no autocomplete or other mechanism identifies it, and HTML supports autocomplete (H98). The element fails 1.3.5, and the claim, read in good faith, names that failure (purpose of the name field not programmatically identified) even if the right token may be 'name'.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer newsletter input #newsletter-input-email (type=email, name=newsletter, label 'Digite seu e-mail'), asking for the visitor's own e-mail to subscribe. The snapshot and the live server-rendered HTML (fetched 2026-11-25) match: no autocomplete attribute. The skeptic's candidate reason, that type=email identifies the purpose, does not hold: the input type gives the data format, not that the value is the user's own e-mail; WCAG's sufficient technique is the autocomplete token (H98) and type is not listed in Understanding 1.3.5. No other mechanism identifies the purpose, so the element fails 1.3.5 and the claim states that failure exactly.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header wishlist icon (a heart, per the crop), the only content of a link to /account#/wishlist; its alt is the full asset URL '.../whishlist-icon-lojasrede___53704b35...svg', which becomes the link's name. The live server-rendered HTML fetched on 2026-11-25 has the same alt, and the link has no title, aria-label or other text in either (the CMS config has an 'attributeTitle' 'Wishlist Lojas Rede' that is not rendered), so the capture does not differ; the full-page screenshot shows the header area blank, a stitching artefact of the header that does not touch the alt. The only skeptic angle, that the URL contains 'whishlist-icon', does not cure it: F30 names file names as text alternatives that are not alternatives, and H30 requires the alternative of a link's only image to describe the link's function, which a long asset URL with a hash read aloud does not do. The element fails 1.1.1 and the claim names that failure.
